name: vix_filtered_index_trend_v124
author: claude_strategist
mechanism: When India VIX spikes above 21, NIFTY's intraday order flow shifts from retail-dominated mean-reverting noise to sustained institutional directional flow — FIIs either aggressively de-risking or accumulating in bulk. In this regime, the 60-second EMA crossing above the 5-minute EMA on NIFTY signals the onset of one of these institutional waves, confirmed by price trading above session VWAP (day's dominant direction). At 5-second resolution, we enter at the first crossover bar rather than waiting for a full 1-minute confirmation, capturing 20-40% more of the initial impulse before algorithmic followers pile in. The VIX ceiling at 35 avoids extreme panic conditions where NIFTY gaps erratically and limit-order fills become unreliable.

indicators.name: ema_fast_12
indicators.purpose: 60-second fast EMA — trade TRIGGER. Not a 12x blind scale of original EMA(9). The original 9-minute EMA was the slow context filter there; here EMA(12) = 60s serves as the FAST trigger because we're catching the START of the institutional wave, not a multi-minute trend. Needs only 1 minute of data before it stabilizes.

indicators.name: ema_slow_60
indicators.purpose: 5-minute slow EMA — context FILTER. Represents the prevailing short-term trend direction on NIFTY. Crossover of fast above slow signals direction change aligned with fresh institutional interest. 5 minutes is the appropriate slow anchor for a 30-90 second trade — long enough to define trend, short enough to not lag major turns by several minutes.

indicators.name: vwap
indicators.purpose: Session VWAP — cumulative from 09:15. No scaling needed; VWAP is always session-cumulative. Confirms that the EMA crossover is aligned with the day's dominant institutional direction (buy-side accumulation vs distribution). Filters crossovers that fight the day's flow.

indicators.name: india_vix
indicators.purpose: Regime filter: VIX > 21 selects sessions where FII/institutional directional orders dominate over retail mean-reversion. VIX ceiling at 35 avoids extreme panic where NIFTY gaps erratically and short-term EMA signals whipsaw. The 21 threshold matches the original strategy directly — it represents the transition point where implied volatility pricing reflects genuine institutional positioning rather than routine noise.

conditions: EMA(12) crosses ABOVE EMA(60) — bullish crossover on current bar
close > session_VWAP — trade in direction of day's dominant flow
buy_ce.confirmation: All conditions on same 5-second bar; crossover detected as prev bar fast<slow, current bar fast>slow

conditions: EMA(12) crosses BELOW EMA(60) — bearish crossunder on current bar
close < session_VWAP — confirming bearish bias for the day
buy_pe.confirmation: All conditions on same 5-second bar; crossunder detected as prev bar fast>slow, current bar fast<slow

exit.stop_rationale: In elevated VIX regime (>21), NIFTY's typical noise is 6-10 spot points per minute. A false crossover (regime filter misfire) would retrace 8-12 spot pts quickly — 4 option points (at delta ~0.5) corresponds to ~8 spot pts, stopping us out before the full reversal materializes. This matches the 30-60s hold where a 1-minute NIFTY swing of 8 pts would negate the crossover thesis.
exit.target_rationale: VIX>21 trend impulses on NIFTY typically extend 15-30 spot points in the first 1-2 minutes after an EMA crossover. 7 option points (~14 spot pts at delta 0.5) captures roughly 50-60% of the expected initial leg at 1:1.75 R:R. Targeting beyond 14 spot pts would require holding 2-3 minutes, exceeding our time stop.

filters.vix_filter: 21 <= VIX <= 35 — elevated volatility for institutional flow, ceiling avoids extreme panic
filters.time_filter: 09:30-15:20 IST — skip opening 15 minutes of pre-open noise and price discovery
filters.volume_filter: none — NIFTY index volume is always sufficient
filters.trend_filter: VWAP alignment — only trade crossovers in VWAP-confirmed direction
filters.spread_filter: none — limit orders at close price, no spread cost

edge.edge_decay_risk: medium — VIX threshold of 21 may shift as market structure evolves; institutional behavior in VIX regimes is relatively stable but not permanent

adaptation_notes: Original traded top-50 FnO stocks with EMA(9/21) on 1-minute bars, holding 30-60 minutes. The equity universe was incidental — the signal logic (VIX regime + EMA crossover + VWAP) is purely index-level. Converted: (1) EMA periods compressed from 9-min/21-min to 1-min/5-min because we hold 30-90s not 30-60min — we're catching the ONSET of the institutional wave, not the full trend. (2) VIX thresholds kept identical (21 lower bound) as the regime logic is unchanged. (3) ATR-based stop replaced with fixed 4 option-point stop sized to typical 30-second NIFTY move magnitudes. (4) 90-second time stop replaces original 60-bar (60-min) time stop.
weaknesses: VIX crossings of 21 are relatively infrequent — strategy may have low trade count on many days
EMA crossovers on 5-second NIFTY bars can produce false signals during choppy VIX>21 sessions
VIX data is lagged intraday (forward-filled at 5s); VIX can spike suddenly post-event
High-VIX sessions often have larger gap-opens — VWAP may be anchored far from current price
